title: Build-time guard lives in setup.py, never in the generated pyproject.toml
answers: add a check to pyproject.toml for the skinny build
where to put build validation for libs/skinny
pyproject.toml is generated, can I edit it to fail the build
setuptools hook to validate the mlflow symlink
body:
Invariant: libs/skinny/pyproject.toml and libs/tracing/pyproject.toml are generated by dev/pyproject.py and marked do-not-edit; any build-time check must go in the sibling setup.py.
Enforced at: libs/skinny/setup.py and libs/tracing/setup.py (module-level guard, then bare setup()).
What breaks if skipped: hand edits to pyproject.toml are overwritten on regeneration. setuptools still executes setup.py when it sits beside PEP 621 metadata, so the guard runs without changing packaging config.
Constraints: Call setup() with no arguments. Passing packaging arguments into setup() would take over metadata and package discovery from pyproject.toml.
applies: Any change to build validation or packaging for libs/skinny and libs/tracing.
says: Build checks added to minimal package configurations get overwritten whenever configs are regenerated.
Where should we place installation validation guards for the lightweight client packages?
Build validation rules disappear after running the automated package configuration generator.
Ensure lightweight package builds abort immediately when packaging environment checks fail.
search: Build-time guards for libs/skinny and libs/tracing must be placed in sibling setup.py files rather than generated pyproject.toml files. Because libs/skinny/pyproject.toml and libs/tracing/pyproject.toml are generated by dev/pyproject.py, manual edits to them are overwritten on regeneration. When adding build validation, execute a module-level guard in setup.py and call setup() with no packaging arguments to preserve metadata discovery from pyproject.toml.
